evals.prompt: Riverside Refugee Resettlement ($3M, Boise) gets about 60% of revenue from federal funds through a state pass-through. We need a new case management software vendor, roughly $45k a year, mostly charged to the federal award. Historically we've just used whoever our ED knows. Write us a procurement policy and walk me through doing this purchase correctly.
evals.expected_output: A tiered procurement policy aligned to existing approval thresholds, the 2 CFR 200 procurement elements for the federally funded purchase, COI disclosure up front, documented selection and contract-clause review, with counsel review.
assertions: Provides a dollar-tiered purchasing policy and ties it to the approval thresholds in financial controls rather than creating a conflicting table
Applies the 2 CFR 200.317-327 procurement standards for the federally funded purchase, including full and open competition and documented cost/price analysis
Tells the user to verify current micro-purchase and simplified acquisition thresholds rather than assuming fixed figures
Requires conflict-of-interest disclosure from everyone involved before selection begins, with recusal
Requires documenting the selection decision and reviewing contract clauses including data ownership and deletion on termination
Recommends counsel review of the policy and contract

evals.prompt: landlord sent our lease renewal. 5,000 sq ft, $24/sq ft, 5 yrs, 4% annual bumps, triple net. our budget occupancy line is $130k. good deal or no?
evals.expected_output: Models total occupancy cost including NNN pass-throughs and escalation against the budget line and suggests nonprofit-favorable terms to negotiate, with counsel review.
assertions: Models total occupancy cost including CAM, property tax and insurance pass-throughs, not just base rent
Shows base rent alone is about $120k in year one and escalates annually, and compares the total to the $130k budget line
Suggests negotiating terms such as capped escalation, tenant improvement allowance or early termination tied to funding

evals.prompt: Our building needs a new roof, about $180k. The plan is to put it in next year's operating budget as a repair expense. Also, our board president's brother-in-law owns a roofing company and has offered us a 'great deal.'
evals.expected_output: Moves the roof out of the operating budget as a capital expenditure with a dedicated funding source, and requires COI disclosure, recusal and competitive bids for the related-party offer.
assertions: Treats the roof as a capital expenditure kept out of the operating budget
Suggests funding from a capital campaign, designated capital reserve or specific grant
Requires the board president to disclose the conflict and be recused from selection
Requires competitive bids at this dollar level and documentation of the selection
Coordinates with reserves/cash-flow planning if reserves fund it

should_not_trigger.query: Book a venue and caterer for our spring gala
Set dollar limits for who can approve invoices and sign checks
